title: Price against cost
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Would you pay three times what something costs to make?

groups.heading: The idiot index in real estate

lines.text: I said investors told me over lunch about incredible investments by developers in one city. I was already pessimistic. I asked: what is the final price per square metre of these units?

They said four thousand five hundred a square metre. I said I knew for a fact that banks there were financing construction costs to developers at about twelve hundred. Construction companies in competitive markets make thirty-five to forty percent margins. So add thirty-five or fifty percent to the cost and you see the retail buyers are paying about three times what they should.
That is the idiot index, I said. Why would I ever pay literally three times the cost of something? That is market speculation on the part of a developer.

A student said it is easy to go down the rabbit hole and get lost in an idea. If you are not thinking big picture about what is actually valuable, it could become the demise of the business and the person.

There are many wisdom sayings, I said. One is: making money is discovering value before anybody else does. You can look at a run-down building and see that it needs an architect and a construction company, and that the units could be split, in a great area.
Do the economic study of the comparables, I said: the rents, whether it has parking. Somebody else could be driving past and just see a run-down building.
Some people have such high business intuition that they don't even do the spreadsheets. Their feeling is based on years of experience. They pull the gun out of the holster and shoot, I said.
Even if you have that intuition, I would go to the data and the evidence, I said. The person in the book does the research and goes for the evidence, reading all the time.
When a broker says it is a great investment because of who the developer was, he says: who cares? Maybe it is overpriced. Look at a hundred transactions within five miles. Look at the rents.
What is the price against the cost, and what do a hundred comparables say?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write an investment someone has pitched you.
Write the price and the real cost behind it.
Write the comparables you would look at.
Write the intuition you have and the data that would test it.
Write one thing you could buy at its cost and sell at its value.

check.q: What did I ask the investors about the units?
choices: The final price per square metre

check.q: What did I say making money is?
choices: Discovering value before anybody else does

check.q: What would I do even with a strong intuition?
choices: Go to the data and the evidence

recap: Compare price to cost. Back your intuition with data.
